items.overall_experience: The online assessment had 2 coding questions (DP and Graph BFS) plus an Amazon Leadership Principles behavioral evaluation. Round 1 and 2 were technical with deep dive into system design basics and data structures. Round 3 was bar raiser with the hiring manager discussing trade-offs.
questions_asked: Design a high-throughput URL shortener with low latency caching
Find the shortest path in a weighted grid with dynamic obstacle elimination
Tell me about a time you had to make a decision without complete data
items.tips_for_juniors: Master Amazon 16 Leadership Principles with STAR format examples. For technical rounds, practice explaining your thought process out loud before writing any code on the shared editor.

items.overall_experience: Initial screening on HackerEarth followed by 3 rounds of 45-minute Google Meet coding interviews. Every round started with a warm-up string/array question and quickly scaled to tree traversals and dynamic programming optimization.
questions_asked: Implement Trie with prefix search and wildcard match
Given stream of integers, output the median in real-time with O(log N) insert
Detect cycle in directed graph using Kahn's algorithm
items.tips_for_juniors: Clean modular code and time/space complexity analysis matter as much as solving the problem. Do not rush into coding; clarify edge cases first.

items.overall_experience: Round 1 was quantitative aptitude and SQL debugging. Round 2 was technical interview with focus on REST APIs, relational databases, and my final year capstone project. Round 3 was partner interview focused on client consulting scenarios.
questions_asked: Difference between inner join, outer join, and cross join with practical examples
Explain ACID properties and how PostgreSQL ensures isolation
How would you explain cloud microservices to a non-technical client?
items.tips_for_juniors: Prepare your resume projects thoroughly. Be ready to justify why you chose specific libraries or tech stack over alternatives.

items.overall_experience: NQT Exam had Advanced Coding section with 2 problems (Matrix manipulation and Greedy approach). The interview was conducted on TCS iON platform with 3 panelists (Technical, Managerial, HR) questioning simultaneously.
questions_asked: Write code to reverse linked list in groups of K
Difference between monolithic and microservices architecture
Are you willing to relocate across India?
items.tips_for_juniors: Score high in NQT Advanced Section to get upgraded to Digital/Prime package interviews instead of standard Ninja track.

items.overall_experience: HackWithInfy contest qualified candidates for the SP role. Round 1 coding had 3 tough competitive programming problems. Interview had live whiteboard problem solving on graphs and dynamic programming.
questions_asked: Longest Increasing Subsequence in O(N log N) using binary search
Bridges in an undirected graph using Tarjan's algorithm
items.tips_for_juniors: Focus on standard competitive programming algorithms like Segment Trees and Fenwick Trees to crack the 9.5 LPA SP band.

items.overall_experience: Reached Round 3. Round 1 and 2 went exceptionally well with binary tree questions and caching logic. Round 3 focused heavily on OS concurrency and low-level thread synchronization where I struggled with deadlocks.
questions_asked: Serialize and deserialize a binary tree with negative values
Implement thread-safe Producer-Consumer queue with condition variables
items.tips_for_juniors: Do not ignore core computer science fundamentals (OS, Concurrency, DBMS internals). Top-tier product companies test system depth.
